name: When should I consider replacing the entire toilet instead of just repairing a running toilet?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider replacing the entire toilet instead of just repairing a running toilet?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider replacing the entire toilet if it's very old, has visible cracks in the tank or bowl, frequently clogs, or requires multiple, repeated repairs. While a running toilet can often be fixed with a simple component replacement, a consistently problematic or inefficient toilet might be costing you more in water waste and repair bills over time. Upgrading to a modern, high-efficiency toilet can significantly reduce water consumption and improve flushing performance, especially if your current toilet is an older, water-guzzling model.
acceptedAnswer.description: Consider replacing the toilet if it's old, cracked, clogs often, or needs frequent repairs. A new, high-efficiency model can save water and improve performance.
